description: Evidence-bounded recipe for a second South Division parcel: the South Water and Lake commercial belt, its rear service yards, one western mixed block, and loose development between Randolph and Washington. Every slot is an anonymous recommendation, not a recovered building or parcel.

coordinate_system.bearing: degrees clockwise from north; facade faces the named frontage
coordinate_system.note: Street and lot geometry are measured from the 1834 Wright and Hathaway plats through the committed datum. Neither plat depicts buildings. Slot centers, setback, facade bearing and occupancy are interpretive. The 20 m value is the existing datum's working georeference uncertainty, not parcel evidence.

inventory.counting_rule: Do not add these 84 to the scene count until existing named and compound roofs have been reconciled. A better-evidenced roof substitutes for a slot; it never increases the 665 target.

aggregate_mix.basis: The owner reconstruction specification supplies the 665-roof family schedule and a South Division group target of 370 roofs, including 42 stores, 17 freight roofs and 15 workshops.

street_grid.basis: The 1834 Wright survey and Hathaway plat supply streets, blocks and lots. Their committed affine georeference has 17.5 m RMS residual; neither map supplies a roof footprint.

commercial_continuity.basis: Andreas preserves a South Water address described by doors and a 55 ft lot width; existing project dossiers interpret this as evidence of a legible run of premises, not proof of any anonymous slot.

individual_slots.basis: No supplied building census, tax improvement roll, fire-insurance plan or period footprint map identifies these roofs.

clusters.rationale: Narrow commercial and mixed-use slots occupy only the measured gaps between the project's protected named South Water records. The row is discontinuous: named buildings, alleys, yards and open gaps remain visible.
overlap_controls: Centers are assigned to frontage gaps after reserving envelopes around Newberry & Dole, Temple, J. H. Kinzie, H. Jones, Carpenter, Peck, Democrat, Loomis, Pruyne & Kimball, Madore Beaubien, Chicago American and Frederick Thomas records.
C4, T2 and other wide footprints remain below the 55 ft period lot-width ceiling only where placed in multi-lot or corner-size gaps.
A later exact oriented-footprint test against every active 1835 phase is mandatory before generation.

clusters.rationale: Freight, trades and service roofs sit behind the mercantile frontage with irregular cargo yards. The second staggered band avoids turning South Water into a single modern-looking wall.
overlap_controls: The -55 m band is separated from the South Water frontage and the -78/-82 m service pair is staggered into selected rear yards.
F3 and F4 slots require terrain-pad review and at least 10 ft clear working aprons; they must move or substitute rather than overlap a protected record.
Ancillary roofs are paired to yard groups at implementation and must not be counted as independent street-front premises.

clusters.frontage: Lake Street north side and eastern transition
clusters.rationale: A mixed sequence of deep-plan houses, improved houses, store-residences and one public house fills selected Lake Street gaps without duplicating the protected Sauganash, Exchange, Old Bank, churches, Tremont, Mansion House or Dole records.
overlap_controls: The row reserves generous envelopes around every named Lake Street phase and retains open ground around St. Mary's and First Presbyterian.
The 840 m eastern transition slot is east of State but remains inside the currently modelled South/Fort approach; it is not evidence of a dense eastern extension.
Lake/La Salle wet-ground interpretation must be checked against the visible terrain before any foundation is generated.

clusters.frontage: block between Market and Franklin, Lake and Randolph
clusters.rationale: Four narrow lot columns hold a loose mixture of ordinary houses, a joiner shop, one larger house and rear service roofs. The block steps down sharply from Lake Street intensity.
overlap_controls: The north band remains south of the protected Sauganash/Hogan/Philo Carpenter group; no slot claims their parcel.
Rows are separated by roughly 35 m and leave about half the block area open for yards, tracks and wet ground.
Rear A-family roofs must be assigned to a principal yard group before count adoption.

clusters.frontage: selected blocks between Randolph and Washington
clusters.rationale: Ordinary houses and a few improved or public-service roofs form three discontinuous bands. Development deliberately skips the Public Square and leaves entire lot runs vacant so the enlarged plat does not read as a fully occupied city.
overlap_controls: No slot is placed from local E 445-595 in the north band, preserving the Public Square and the protected jail/courthouse-construction records.
The estray-pen envelope near local E 469, N -377 remains clear; the southern bands split west and east of it.
The recipe ends at Washington Street. It makes no South Division extent claim beyond the currently controlled street/terrain envelope.

adoption_gates: Reconcile every existing 1835 structure record to physical roof units before decrementing the South target.
Run an oriented-footprint collision test against every protected existing and phase-one footprint, including compound sub-roofs.
Reject or move any footprint whose sampled terrain corners include water, exceed the walkable pad slope, or overlap the visible street track.
Pair each A-family roof with a principal-yard group and verify that its count remains ancillary.
Create one explicit liberty entry covering each adopted slot's existence, position and footprint; label all generated assets as inferred/placeholder until family geometry is canonical.
